appearance.bodies.stem.ribs.count.why: A stem's ribs vary within the count its flora gives; the body draws more of them round a thicker stem.

appearance.bodies.stem.areoles.spacing.why: Areoles sit along a rib's crest, or over a joint, this far apart.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.radial.cou.why: An areole bears as many radial spines as its flora counts, varying within its range.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.radial.len.why: Floras give the longest spines; a set's spines vary a quarter either way about its length, so the longest stand about a quarter above it.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.central.co.why: An areole bears as many central spines as its flora counts. Where one central stands apart as the main one, the others are set by hand, so the two sets together make the count.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.central.le.why: As for the radials: the longest central stands about a quarter above the set's length.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.main.lengt.why: The main central is the longest a flora gives, about a quarter above its set's length.

traits.spines.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, p. 8): every cactus has areoles, special organs in the axils of its leaves or where they would be, which bear its spines (and glochids, hairs or glands), its branches and its flowers.

traits.note: Abrams's Illustrated Flora of the Pacific States, volume 3 (1951), read in full (Cactaceae by I. L. Wiggins): perianth segments numerous, grading from sepals to petals, imbricated, their bases coalescent in a cup or tube borne on the apex of the ovary; stamens numerous, on the throat of the tube; ovary inferior, 1-celled; style 1, stigma lobes 1 to numerous. Jepson eFlora (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): flowers radial, rarely bilateral. No flora counts the tepals.

generator.program.note: The cacti's own program (growth plan G2.3a): columns, barrels and chains of joints, their ribs, areoles and spines from each species' look.

rules.note: Spec rework E6c: the cacti's ribs, areoles and spines grown from the characters their floras state, in each body look that has ribs or a spine set of that role.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Cactaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 375, 376, family Cactaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral; read as "spiral".

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 375, 376, family Cactaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.inflorescence.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 375, 376, family Cactaceae: inflorescence solitary flowers in the axils (rarely terminal cymes), usually; read as {"solitary": "usually"}.

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 375, 376, family Cactaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite (rarely unisexual), usually; read as {"hermaphrodite": "usually"}.

traits.fruit_type.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 374, 375, 376, family Cactaceae: fruit type berry (rarely dry and indehiscent), usually; read as {"berry": "usually"}.
